messages.subject: Re-calibration with internal calibrants
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

is there any method to do re-calibration of mz-values with the help of internal calibrants in Cardinal? Or any other free-software package enabling this?

Thanks,
Melanie

If you have a link to an article describing a method for the re-calibration you'd like, it could help me possible implement such a method in the future.

Thanks,
Kylie

messages.subject: Re: reduceDimension classifying
messages.body_plain:
Hi Paco,

Sorry for taking so long to get to replying to this.

For binning you can say, if it says m/z 456, it represents the range m/z 456 +/- (width/2) where the window was set during the binning process. The current default width is 200 ppm, so 456 +/- (100 ppm), or 456 +/- 0.0456. (Or whatever you set the bin width to.)

For resampling, it's not quite so simple, because it uses linear interpolation. So rather than representing a range of m/z values, it represents a prediction of what the intensity would be at that exact m/z value (e.g., 456), if a measurement were taken at that m/z value, calculated from the next-closest m/z points at which intensities were measured.

-Kylie

messages.subject: Re: error in combine method
messages.body_plain:
Hi Paco,

That is a rather roundabout error message, but my best guess is that it's due to the fact that batchProcess() is trying to be helpful by automatically calculating the mean spectrum and saving it to the output's featureData, and the default combine() method for AnnotatedDataFrames fails when it encounters shared columns (in this case, mean spectra) that don't match.

I will make a note to either make outputting the mean spectrum optional, or make some changes so that such an error message is more helpful in the future.

For now, the easy solution is to do:

fData(object)$mean <- NULL

for each MSImageSet object you want to combine. That'll remove the offending columns, and hopefully combine() should work again.

-Kylie
